name: Yuhyun Lee
status: Open to postdoctoral & industry R&D opportunities
hero_intro: a Ph.D. candidate working at the intersection of neural stimulation, electrophysiology, and experimental systems engineering.
hero_body: I build preclinical platforms, study how electric fields recruit neural activity, and turn complex experiments into reproducible quantitative evidence—with the long-term goal of translating neurotechnology beyond the lab.
meta_description: Yuhyun Lee is a Biomedical Engineering Ph.D. candidate at Carnegie Mellon University building preclinical neural stimulation and electrophysiology platforms.
about_paragraph_1: I began by creating EEG tools for zebrafish and moved into electrical stimulation and multi-channel neural recording in mice. Working across models has shaped how I think about the strengths—and limits—of each experimental approach.
about_paragraph_2: I'm interested in teams developing neural interfaces, adaptive stimulation, neuroprosthetics, and translational neurotechnology, where rigorous experiments and engineering can move new ideas closer to meaningful use.
conference_text: IEEE BRAIN Discovery and Neurotechnology Workshop · Society for Neuroscience (SfN), Washington, DC
contact_body: I'm exploring postdoctoral and industry R&D opportunities in neural engineering, preclinical neurotechnology, and neural-interface development. I'd be glad to discuss a research question or a potential collaboration.
contact_card: Research collaborations, postdoctoral roles, and neurotechnology R&D teams.
